conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option<String> or Vec<String>, never Result (ExtractInheritanceHandler = fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String>). Source slicing is bounds-checked via get_node_text(node, source) -> Option<String> (languages/mod.rs). Engine-level failures use ParserError (QueryError, UnsupportedLanguage, ParseError, Timeout). Java and Swift handlers return empty Vec for absent clauses rather than erroring.

patterns: Per-language module exposes &'static str consts ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY (java.rs lines 4-38; swift.rs lines 6-38).
LanguageInfo holds grammar Language plus query strings and Option handler fn pointers; a language sets None for slots it does not use (css.rs, markdown and yaml arms in mod.rs).
Java extract_inheritance reads child_by_field_name('superclass') and child_by_field_name('interfaces'), then prefixes 'extends ' and 'implements ' (java.rs 131-165).

Swift extract_inheritance walks node.child(i) for kind 'inheritance_specifier', takes named_child(0), and labels the first base 'extends' and later ones 'conforms' (swift.rs 49-80). This is the closest precedent for PHP, whose clauses are unnamed-field children.

Capture-name contract consumed by parser_elements.rs: 'function', 'class', 'func_name'/'method_name', 'class_name'/'type_name' (element); 'call' (call); 'import_path' (import); 'type_ref' (reference); 'write.*', 'read.*', 'writeread.*' prefixes (defuse). Queries that use other names produce no output for that feature.

Defuse dedupe: a read capture at the same start byte as a write/writeread capture is dropped (parser_elements.rs ~870-900). PHP's variable_name is both the LHS write and the read, so this dedupe is load-bearing.
Lazy per-language QUERY_CACHE keyed by supported_languages() names (parser.rs 192-245).
Inline test helper per language: parse_<lang>(src) -> Tree, then stack traversal to locate a node kind (java.rs tests; swift.rs tests).

Wiring precedent for a new language is the css/swift arm set: pub mod line, get_language_info arm, get_ts_language arm, EXTENSION_MAP entry, supported_languages entry, workspace and crate Cargo entries, README list. See wiring_summary.

approaches.name: A. Java-template full handler on LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, enum), CALL_QUERY (function, member, scoped calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (type-ref via name nodes), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name writes and reads, Java-shaped), and extract_inheritance that walks named children for base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements). Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP so mixed HTML parses. Wire mod.rs (pub mod php, get_language_info arm with extract_inheritance: Some(php::extract_inheritance) and defuse Some, get_ts_language arm), lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP ('php','php'), supported_languages), Cargo entries, Cargo.lock, README. Inline tests plus one integration test.
pros: Meets every acceptance item in #1864, including DEFUSE_QUERY and mixed-HTML zero-ERROR behaviour.
Follows java.rs and swift.rs shape exactly; reviewers can diff against them.
LANGUAGE_PHP handles <?php blocks inside HTML without ERROR nodes, which the issue requires.
cons: Several node kinds and field names are unconfirmed against node-types.json (trait_declaration, namespace_use_declaration, assignment_expression fields, member_call_expression name label); each needs a compile-test check.
Defuse on PHP variable_name needs the start-byte dedupe to avoid double counting, and the behaviour must be tested.
Largest change set of the three approaches.

approaches.name: B. Thin handler without DEFUSE_QUERY, PHP_ONLY grammar
approaches.description: php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance only; defuse_query: None in mod.rs, the way fortran, css and markdown do. Use the pure-PHP entry point (LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, name unconfirmed) so the grammar tree is simpler.
pros: Fewest unconfirmed node kinds (no assignment or parameter kinds to verify).
Smallest diff; quickest path to a green CI.
Simplest inheritance walk on the pure-PHP tree.
cons: Violates the issue: DEFUSE_QUERY is a named required constant, and the acceptance list does not allow omitting it.
PHP_ONLY cannot parse mixed HTML/PHP files without ERROR nodes, failing the explicit HTML-template acceptance item.
Leaves analyze_symbol def-use empty for PHP, which users will notice.

approaches.name: C. Query-driven inheritance and compiled-once query table
approaches.description: Same five queries as A, but extract_inheritance runs a compiled tree-sitter Query (base_clause and class_interface_clause captures) held in a OnceLock inside php.rs, rather than a hand-written child walk. Wiring identical to A.
pros: Declarative and consistent with how the other capture-based features work.
Easier to extend later to trait use or interface extends without new walk code.
cons: Adds a sixth query and a static OnceLock, beyond the five-constant contract the issue asks for.
Query output ordering and duplicate matches need explicit handling to keep the required ['extends Bar', 'implements A', 'implements B'] order.
Extra complexity for one function; a reviewer may ask for the child walk used by swift.rs instead.

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only one that meets every acceptance item in #1864 (DEFUSE_QUERY present, LANGUAGE_PHP for mixed HTML, both extends and implements). It copies the java.rs query shape and the swift.rs child-walk inheritance, so it adds the least new design. Before writing code, run Query::new on each draft query inside a unit test (the issue's step 3) to settle the unconfirmed node kinds. Pick the tree-sitter-php crate version on crates.io against tree-sitter 0.27.x and confirm the constant name LANGUAGE_PHP. Add php to supported_languages() as well as to get_language_info, or PHP parsing will fail at the QUERY_CACHE lookup.

element_query_draft:
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class

Notes: function_definition (top-level function) and method_declaration are confirmed by the Context7 corpus s-expressions with name: (name). interface_declaration name, enum_declaration name, class_declaration name are confirmed by Context7 grammar and node-types excerpts. trait_declaration is NOT confirmed and must pass the compile test. Capture names follow parser_elements.rs contract (function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name).
defuse_query_draft:
(simple_parameter
  name: (variable_name) @write.local)
(assignment_expression
  left: (variable_name) @write.assign)
(augmented_assignment_expression
  left: (variable_name) @writeread.update)
(update_expression
  (variable_name) @writeread.update)
(variable_name) @read.usage

Adapted from java.rs DEFUSE_QUERY (local_variable_declaration -> write.local, assignment_expression -> write.assign, update_expression -> writeread.update, identifier -> read.usage). PHP has no local declaration keyword, so the write.local analogue is a parameter declaration; a first assignment is covered by write.assign. variable_name wraps name (confirmed by corpus '(variable_name (name))'). Unconfirmed: simple_parameter name field, assignment_expression left field, augmented_assignment_expression, update_expression. The read.usage pattern also matches LHS nodes; parser_elements.rs drops those reads when a write capture has the same start byte.
inheritance_walk_citation:
Source: tree-sitter-php grammar, as served by Context7 from github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php: common/define-grammar.js and php/src/node-types.json (the literal pinned file was NOT fetched; gh was refused for this repository). Field-by-field walk from a class_declaration node:
(1) class_declaration has fields attributes (optional attribute_list), name (required, type name), body (required, declaration_list). It has NO superclass, interfaces, parent_class, base_classes fields; the Context7 excerpt states these names do not exist in this grammar. So child_by_field_name('superclass') and ('interfaces') return None for PHP, unlike Java.
(2) base_clause is not a field. Grammar rule: base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). Find it by iterating named children of the class_declaration and matching kind 'base_clause'. Each named child of base_clause is a class name; Context7 corpus shows (name) for these. Push format!("extends {text}") per name.
(3) class_interface_clause is not a field. Grammar rule: class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). Find by iterating named children and matching kind 'class_interface_clause'. Corpus confirms the shape '(class_declaration name: (name) (class_interface_clause (name)) body: (declaration_list ...))'. Push format!("implements {text}") per name.
(4) body (declaration_list) holds methods and properties and is not walked.
(5) No clauses: no base_clause or class_interface_clause child, so the result is an empty Vec.
Unconfirmed: whether _name can resolve to qualified_name for namespaced bases (accept both kinds to be safe); whether interface_declaration uses base_clause for extends (not checked).
